attempts.paper_title: New information triggers prospective codes to adapt for flexible navigation
attempts.entry_title: Prospective goal codes in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex (Prince et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The paragraph is below for you to save: Most behavioral and CA1 findings held up in this data, but the prefrontal choice findings could not be tested and some claims of no difference did not hold. CA1 decoding of both goal arms rose on switch trials after the update cue, and goal coding was stronger in CA1 than in prefrontal cortex. The prefrontal switch from old to new choice could not be tested, because the movement-based choice estimate would take about 10 hours to compute. Prefrontal goal-arm decoding rose slightly on switch trials, which the paper reports as absent, and in the first theta half cycle central-arm decoding exceeded goal arms, where the paper reports the opposite.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Prince, Cushing, Yassine, Katragadda, Roberts and Singer (2025) on dandiset 001371, which holds the units, behaviour and LFP of 66 sessions from 7 mice in a virtual y-maze task with switch and stay cues. It tests the behaviour, Bayesian position decoding in CA1 and prefrontal cortex around the update cue, its theta phase, the residual goal codes on correct and incorrect trials, and their relation to view angle. The LSTM choice estimate and the choice decoding built on it were timed and do not fit the notebook limit.

findings.statement: The units tables of five sessions (S20-210517, S28-211114, S29-211104, S29-211105, S34-220617; 633 units) hold only the phy columns, with no region, cell type, electrodes or electrode group column (61 of the 66 units tables have an electrode group). Their ch values (0 to 63) do not say which of the two 64-channel probes a unit is on, since ch runs from 0 to 63 on both probes in the labelled sessions, so they cannot be assigned to CA1 or PFC. With them, the unit count equals the paper's 6449; without them, CA1 has 3545 units and PFC 2271 against 3892 and 2557.
Position (processing/behavior/position) is labelled meters, but its values are in virtual track units (y from -117 to 286, the code's track ends at 285).
View angle is labelled degrees, but its values run from -1.047 to 1.047, radians (plus or minus 60 degrees).
The theta phase in processing/ecephys/decomposition_phase is labelled degrees, but its values run from -pi to pi, radians.

The trials column turn_type is described as {'right': 1, 'left': 2}. In the data, correct delay only trials with turn_type 1 all end at negative x (2521 of 2521) and have choice 1, and the paper's code maps turn_type 1 to left and puts the left arm at negative x; the description has the two labels the other way round, or names sides by a convention the files do not state.

The Methods and the Figure 1b legend give rolling windows of 40 trials, but the reported window counts (6252 delay only, 1002 switch, 117 stay) are those of 15-trial windows, the code's default; 40-trial windows give 4636, 239 and none.

Supplementary Table 1 lists 8104 delay trials; the final-task delay only trials number 7172, the Results' count, and the 932 warm-up trials (maze_id 3) make up the difference. The trial-type fractions of the Results (65, 25 and 10%) are not those of the trials (0.737, 0.189, 0.074).

The paper's code counts the encoder training trials (80% of delay only trials) for the 50-trial session rule, where the Methods count the trials of the session; on this dataset the Methods' count gives 55 CA1 and 46 PFC sessions, close to the 56 and 47 of Supplementary Table 2, and the code's count 47 and 37. A reader amended S1 to follow the Methods (answer of 2026-11-02), and the code's count changes two outcomes here (sfig3c-retrospective-unchanged, p = 0.14 against 0.036, and sfig12-delay-hpc-no-outcome-difference, p = 0.096 against 0.043).

The paper's code reads the theta phase stored in the file (general/lfp.py), where the Methods describe a phase from peaks and troughs of the filtered LFP; the two agree closely at the decoding bins (mean cosine of their difference, median 0.975 over 59 sessions), and every theta outcome is the same with either. In the session where they agree least (S20-210511, mean cosine -0.49) the pyramidal spikes are barely locked to theta (0.085 and 0.086 of spikes in the peak 30-degree bin against 0.083 for uniform firing), so the reference phase of maximal firing, and with it the referenced phase, is nearly arbitrary under either estimate.

The Methods define the decoding spread of Supplementary Fig. 5f by "how far in front and behind of the peak value the decoding results dropped below this threshold" (peak minus one standard deviation), the first crossing on each side; the paper's code (plot_region_error_distribution) takes the outermost bins at or above the threshold anywhere before and after the peak. On this dataset the first crossing gives 0.14 and 0.37 bins (CA1, PFC) and the code's rule 4.07 and 4.37, against the paper's 2.4 and 3.13.

Question for the paper's authors: which 0.2 s bins enter the windows after the update cue (0 to 0.5, 0 to 1 and 0 to 1.5 s)? The code samples the decoding at -2.5, -2.3, ..., -0.1, 0.1, ..., 2.5 s and cuts windows with pd.cut, which this attempt follows; a grid with a bin centred on the cue, counted after it, shifts the windows by 0.1 s. On this dataset the shift changes three outcomes (sfig3c-retrospective-unchanged p = 0.036 against 0.12; fig5d-stay-hpc-below-switch new arm p = 0.0094 against 0.38; fig7c-hpc-commitment-initial-arm p = 0.29 against 0.040). It also changes one test of fig2g-pfc-no-goal-increase (reading b new arm p = 0.030 against 0.066), whose outcome it leaves unchanged, since reading a fails on both grids.

entries.title: Prospective goal codes in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex (Prince et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Prince, Cushing, Yassine, Katragadda, Roberts and Singer (2025) on dandiset 001371, which holds the units, behaviour and LFP of 66 sessions from 7 mice in a virtual y-maze task with switch and stay cues. It tests the behaviour, Bayesian position decoding in CA1 and prefrontal cortex around the update cue, its theta phase, the residual goal codes on correct and incorrect trials, and their relation to view angle. The LSTM choice estimate and the choice decoding built on it were timed and do not fit the notebook limit.
